acceptance.given: An aggregate executes under a configured finite output budget.

oracle.expected: The aggregate output is observed within the configured finite bound and the terminal result records budget compliance.
forbidden: Budget exhaustion is reported as successful completion.
oracle.observable: During runtime verification, inspect aggregate output size and terminal status against the configured bound.

acceptance.then: The aggregate remains within the finite output bound and reaches a deterministic terminal state.
acceptance.when: During aggregate execution, the runtime verifier measures output and evaluates the terminal state.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the aggregate with an output budget and select an execution that exceeds or fails to report the finite bound.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Enforce and observe the aggregate finite output bound and deterministic unsuccessful budget exhaustion.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing aggregate result and terminal-state formats; only add bounded-output enforcement.

slice_hint.state_transition: aggregate executing under budget -> bounded output with deterministic terminal result
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Runtime evidence shows output_size <= configured_output_bound and terminal_state is deterministic; budget exhaustion is unsuccessful.

acceptance.given: An applicable Consumer is at the pre-restoration point of the enable, disable, behavioral rollback, and re-enable flow.

oracle.expected: After the complete flow, the Consumer's verdict and diagnostics equal the established verdict/diagnostic baseline.
forbidden: The completed flow leaves verdict or diagnostic results different from the established baseline.
oracle.observable: Inspect the Consumer result record after re-enable and compare verdict and diagnostics with the captured baseline.

acceptance.then: The applicable Consumer has its verdict and diagnostic baseline restored.
acceptance.when: The flow completes enable, disable, behavioral rollback, and re-enable through the real call surface, then the verification checks the post-flow record.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select an applicable Consumer whose post-re-enable verdict or diagnostics differ from the captured pre-flow baseline.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Verify that the complete Consumer route lifecycle restores the prior verdict and diagnostic baseline.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Keep existing Consumer manifest, verdict, and diagnostic record schemas compatible.

slice_hint.state_transition: pre-restoration Consumer state -> completed lifecycle with restored baseline
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Every applicable Consumer has a post-flow verdict and diagnostic record equal to its established baseline.

acceptance.given: The evaluation package declares the three named evaluation seeds and their provenance metadata.

oracle.expected: Each named evaluation seed is counted exactly once, with provenance, applicability, missing-label, counterexample-or-explicit-absence, and approved non-baseline classification data.
forbidden: Any specified evaluation seed appears zero times.
Any specified evaluation seed appears more than once.
oracle.observable: The package validator enumerates the three named seeds and records count 1 for each.

acceptance.then: The three specified evaluation seeds each have exactly one record.
acceptance.when: During package evaluation, the validator counts each named seed and checks its required metadata.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select a package containing a missing or duplicated named evaluation seed record.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Validate exact-once presence and required provenance metadata for the three named evaluation seeds.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing seed and package metadata schemas while enforcing exact-once validation.

slice_hint.state_transition: seed declarations present with unconstrained counts -> validated exact-once seed records
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Validator reports count == 1 for each of the three named seeds and all required metadata fields are present.

acceptance.given: Six materially distinct Matrix Cases are designated, each with its own fixture/state and attributable evidence context.

oracle.expected: Each of the six Matrix Cases has a completed execution record for an immutable Stable subject.
forbidden: Any of the six Matrix Cases omits Stable-subject execution.
Stable-subject execution is mutable during the Matrix Case run.
oracle.observable: Inspect the six Matrix Case execution records and verify one immutable Stable-subject record per case.

acceptance.then: All six Matrix Cases have executed their immutable Stable subjects.
acceptance.when: When the six Matrix Cases are executed, the matrix verifier checks fixture/state distinctness and immutable Stable-subject execution records.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select a matrix execution in which at least one of the six cases lacks a completed immutable Stable-subject record.

affected_subjects: Stable subject execution across all six materially distinct Matrix Cases
slice_hint.behavior_change: Execute and verify immutable Stable subjects across all six materially distinct Matrix Cases with attributable records.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Retain matrix case, fixture/state, and execution-evidence schema compatibility.

slice_hint.state_transition: six designated Matrix Cases -> six completed immutable Stable-subject execution records
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Exactly six materially distinct Matrix Cases each contain one completed immutable Stable-subject execution record with attributable evidence.
